  STRUCTURAL. Same three causes as GEOM-REVIEW-4's 06:17 WS verdict, confirmed on EN/ES. One sharper finding on (1):
  (1) Setup + slew: the failing endpoints are u_ctl.ap[*] flops on the face OPPOSITE the u_ctl decision state.
    - EN: cal_r[17] at the SE (~170,10) -> ap[23] at the SW corner (~10,5); ~200 um, 17 logic levels, OAI22 slew 164 ps on a 13-fF load.
    - ES: lh[0] at the E edge (~188,100) -> ap[17] at the W edge (~2,110); ~250 um routed, through a BUFx3 driving 32 loads (slew 87) and an AO21x1 driving 21.9 fF (slew 217) + AOI221 (182 ps).
    - In each mirror variant the face that carries ap[] moves, but the u_ctl decision cone stays on the other side. So one combinational cone spans the full strip, and the same broadcast nets cause the ~1.6-2k slew violations.
    Fix in RTL: compute ap[] next to its decision state (cal_r/lh) and send it to the face as a registered hop (+1 cycle with the schedule if no existing stage absorbs it). Add kept per-g_zn copies of cal_r/ctl (<=~64 loads each). No repeater/resize ECO.
  (2) FF hold on outputs (worst ES u_qo_face q[428] -> qo[428]) = IO basis. Bind I per corner (F1/F2); no port buffers.

Put the L3 nodes at quadrant centroids equidistant from node 1, the L4 nodes at the centroids of their 8 taps, leaf legs short and similar. (3) Re-partition the density taps to equal load (merge the <50-sink taps into neighbours; e.g. 250-400 +-15%), and give each L4 node equal summed load. (4) Target <= 20 ps tap-input balance at TT AND FF (owner MSCTS rule). - Outline 86.4x302.4 (aspect 3.5 FAIL), std area 10727 um2, fill .41 even, empty .11.
- 77317 cells: L 44820 / S 13885 / B 18612; INVx1 10560, BUFx3 3311, BUFx2 2687, BUFx6f 1120.

(b) If the slot must stay: a kit-only retry with lower GPL density or cell padding on the u_bout_bq_d column. With only 5 overflows this may close, but the aspect FAIL and the 365-um r2r stay.
I recommend (a). Re-REQ when GRT is 0 at 50 iterations and col_v <=1.0.

WHAT MY FIXED AND WHAT IT DID NOT: horizontal macro detours fell 2,992 -> 238, so the W-face->E-strip crossing class from my 11:40 FAIL is gone. My 11:40 expectation that channel/col_v would end 'well under 1' was WRONG, because the binding limit is VERTICAL capacity inside each strip. With M1-M4 OBS and an M5 ceiling, a vertical wire can use only M3/M5 tracks inside its strip: over a macro, the jog onto M5 would need M4/M6. That gives ~31 um x (27.8 M3 + 20.8 M5 tracks/um) x 0.75 = ~1,130 tracks per strip (estimate, UNCHECKED). OWN cut probe (signal nets with std-cell/partition-pin endpoints above and below a horizontal cut, within one strip; SRAM pins excluded, so E is a lower bound; CHECKED on review/ep_my/geom.tsv): the W strip (tx gearbox, tx_frame 612 -> sd_tx 512) peaks at 1,108 nets at y=112 (658-1,108 over y 69-327); the E strip (rx + SRAM faces) peaks at 643+ nets. Each strip carries a full-height bit-permuting datapath at ~1x its whole vertical supply before local wiring, which matches M3 at 82 % and the tx r2r 540 / 59. PLAN OPTIONS for DIE-HBM-18 (estimate first, per 12.14): (a) split ep_static into a tx core (gearbox, no SRAM) and an rx core (SRAM column + E strip). Each strip then holds one datapath, and the tx core can take a compact outline. (b) Re-aspect the slot so the strips are >=2x wider at the same area: 2 SRAMs per row back-to-back MY|R0 with live faces toward one shared central rx channel, and tx in an N/S band. (c) An M6 ceiling (the M6 jog opens M5 over the macros for verticals) only by COORD ruling, because it costs die M6 (hbm-overflow-core-ceiling-1026). My preference is (a): it removes the cause and does not touch the die layer budget.
